title: work/working go/going do/doing
subtitle: work / to work / working
summary: Choose between the plain verb (work), to + verb (to work) and the -ing form (working) after other words.

lesson.heading: Three forms of the verb
lesson.text: An English verb has three forms that you meet all the time: the plain form **work**, the *to* form **to work** and the *-ing* form **working**. The word in front of the verb tells you which form you need.

lesson.heading: will / can / must etc. + plain verb
rows: I **might phone** you later. **May** I **sit** here?
I **can't meet** you tomorrow. **Could** you **pass** the salt, please?

lesson.heading: do / does / did + plain verb
lesson.text: In questions and negatives we use **do**, **does** and **did**. After them the verb is always the plain form.

lesson.heading: to work / to go / to be
rows: I **have to go** now. Everybody **has to eat**.
Dave **used to work** in a factory.

lesson.heading: working / going / playing
lesson.text: After **am**, **is**, **are** (present continuous) and after **was**, **were** (past continuous) we use the **-ing** form.

examples.text: It was **raining**, so we didn't go out.
What were you **doing** when the phone rang?

lesson.text: Look at the word in front of the verb: after *can/must/did* use **work**, after *want/have/going* use **to work**, after *am/is/are/was/were* use **working**.

exercises.explanation: After can we use the plain verb: Can you phone Paul?
would like + to ...: I'd like to phone Paul.

exercises.prompt: Which form comes after these words: the plain verb, to + verb, or -ing?
It might ___, so take an umbrella with you.
exercises.explanation: After might we use the plain verb: It might rain.

exercises.prompt: What time do you usually ___ up in the morning?
exercises.explanation: After do we use the plain verb: do you get up.
After did we use the plain verb: Did you watch ... ?

exercises.prompt: My friends were ___ for me when I arrived.
You can turn off the radio. I'm not ___ to it.
I'm tired. I don't want ___ out.
exercises.explanation: want + to ...: I don't want to go out.
He's = he is, so we need the -ing form: He's having a bath.

exercises.prompt: I used ___ a car, but I sold it last year.
exercises.explanation: used + to ...: I used to have a car.

exercises.statement: You don't look well. I don't think you should to go to work today.
exercises.explanation: After should we use the plain verb: I don't think you should go to work today.

exercises.prompt: You are asking a friend about her trip. Put the question in order.
exercises.answer: When you go to London, where are you going to stay?
exercises.explanation: going to + plain verb: are you going to stay.
